summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — IDXX +21%, CBRE +6%, HWM +6%, CRH +6%, PNR +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (LITE -19%, MRVL -13%, CIEN -11%, P -10%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: IDXX (+21.19%) — Q3 2026 beat-and-raise reported Nov 2: revenue $1,214M (+10%), EPS $4.01 vs ~$3.82 whisper, FY26 EPS guide raised to $14.96–15.16. Stock had fallen ~7% into the print. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap healthcare diagnostics, not in any strategy's list). It was also a one-day earnings gap, so a post-close or pre-market signal would have been needed, and a gap this size would likely fail a gap or RSI filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 2026 beat-and-raise reported Nov 2: revenue $1,214M (+10%), EPS $4.01 vs ~$3.82 whisper, FY26 EPS guide raised to $14.96–15.16. Stock had fallen ~7% into the print.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap healthcare diagnostics, not in any strategy's list). It was also a one-day earnings gap, so a post-close or pre-market signal would have been needed, and a gap this size would likely fail a gap or RSI filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gap-continuation rule that admits any US name with S&P 500-level liquidity (e.g. avg dollar volume above $100M) gapping ≥+8% on ≥2× volume the morning after results, even if it isn't in a strategy's static universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed CBRE-specific news today. Q3 earnings were Oct 22. The +6.5% move looks like a rebound in rate-sensitive real estate as Treasury yields fell, from a stock still ~20% below its February high.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CBRE is a mid/large-cap commercial real estate services name that no strategy includes. With no pre-market catalyst or gap, a news-reactive or gap-up screen would not have flagged it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rate-sensitive sector basket (CBRE, JLL, REITs) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a ≥1% daily drop in the 10-year yield, so yield-driven real estate rebounds can be traded.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear same-day news found. Likely a continued rebound after the Oct 29 Q3 beat (revenue +29% to $2.7B, adj. EPS $1.46 vs ~$1.37, FY26 guidance raised, $5B buyback added), with the stock still well below its $310 high.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HWM is a large-cap aerospace supplier that no strategy lists. The catalyst was also stale (earnings 3 trading days earlier), so a news-reactive or gap-up filter would not have fired on Nov 3.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap industrials/aerospace (HWM, GE, TDG) to the momentum universe, and add a post-earnings-drift rule that admits names within 5 trading days of a beat-and-raise when the daily move is ≥ +4% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. CRH's Q3 results date is unconfirmed (sources say Nov 3-9), and nothing shows an earnings release or deal today. Likely an earnings-anticipation or building-materials sector rebound after a ~16% slide since July.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRH is a ~$65B large-cap building-materials name (Irish-domiciled, NYSE primary listing) that no strategy's universe list includes. A +6% gap on no clear news also wouldn't trip a news-reactive trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a universe-expansion rule that auto-includes US-listed materials/industrials names with market cap >$20B and ADV >$200M, so large-cap non-US-domiciled names like CRH get screened by the momentum gap-up filter.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news found; likely continued post-earnings drift after the Oct 27 Q3 beat (adj EPS $1.18 vs ~$1.07 est, ~12% jump that day) and a rebound in industrial/housing-related names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: PNR is a ~$11-12B mid-cap industrial/water-pool equipment name. With no catalyst today, a +6% drift day would not trip news-reactive triggers, and the post-earnings gap came a week earlier.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift (PEAD) watchlist: for 10 trading days after an earnings gap ≥ +8%, admit mid-cap names (>$5B) to the momentum universe, with entry on a ≥ +3% day on ≥ 1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found; SHW rose with a broad rotation out of tech into cyclicals and housing-linked names (Home Depot also up), with oil sharply lower. This is a sector-rotation move, not an earnings or M&A event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SHW is a large-cap industrial/materials name that no strategy covers. With no earnings or news trigger, a news-reactive bot had no signal, and a +6% gap would likely trip a gap/RSI filter anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap cyclicals such as SHW, HD and LOW to the momentum universe, and add a sector-rotation trigger: enter when the sector ETF is up ≥2% and the name gaps ≥3% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in a ~$115B all-stock deal (4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share). MRVL fell ~12.7% and AI-optics stocks sold off, so LITE dropped ~18.6%. Sources date the drop to Nov 2, one day before the bot's date.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LITE is a ~$50B+ AI-optics name. It is now a merger-arb target whose price is pegged to Marvell's, and the drop was a gap on deal news that pre-market positioning would have captured. A momentum or mean-reversion filter would also see no tradable setup.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a pending-M&A-target exclusion/flag (stock-for-stock deal, price tracking acquirer ratio) and, if the bot is long-only, treat acquirer deal-day gaps as a news-reactive skip. Otherwise no actionable change, since profiting from the fall would need shorting.

top_movers.catalyst: Marvell announced a ~$115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum (Lumentum -18.6%), and the move landed amid a broad AI-chip selloff (SOX -3%+) over AI-return doubts.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MRVL is a large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy covers. The drop was also a gap-down on M&A and sector news, which long-only momentum and mean-reversion filters would skip.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis (MRVL, AVGO, AMD) to the news-reactive universe, and flag an acquirer gap-down ≤ -8% on a deal announcement as an event signal, e.g. a mean-reversion watch after 2 sessions.

top_movers.catalyst: Optical/AI-networking sector selloff after Marvell's ~$115B all-stock Lumentum deal raised AI-spending doubts; CIEN fell with peers. I found no CIEN-specific news, and the search sources' dates are ambiguous.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CIEN is a ~$40B+ mid/large-cap optical-networking name that no strategy's universe includes. The move was a sector-wide, news-driven drop, and the bot is long-only, so a falling name gives no entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-contagion rule that flags the optical/AI-networking basket (CIEN, LITE, COHR) when ≥3 names drop ≥8% in a day, and queue the survivors for a next-day mean-reversion watchlist with an RSI<30 gate.

top_movers.catalyst: Everpure (NYSE: P, formerly Pure Storage) fell ~10% in a broad AI/tech sell-off that hit Nasdaq names despite strong guidance. I found no company-specific news, and the date is only loosely confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a ~$39B mid-cap data-storage name, likely excluded by cap or sector filters. The drop was a sector-driven gap-down, so momentum and mean-reversion filters would also have rejected it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a tech/AI-infrastructure basket (P, DELL, LITE) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on Nasdaq down ≥3% over 3 days plus a single-name gap ≤-8%, to catch sell-off rebounds.
